2:199.occasion: Quraysh and their allies stayed at Muzdalifah while other pilgrims stood at Arafat, claiming special status as custodians of the sanctuary. Aishah explains that this command required them to stand at Arafat with everyone else, ending that distinction.
2:199.source: Ibn Kathir on 2:199; Al-Bukhari, report of Aishah

2:220.occasion: Fearing the warnings against consuming orphan property, guardians separated the orphans' meals from their own; leftovers sometimes spoiled. Ibn Abbas reports that this verse permitted sharing food and drink, replacing burdensome separation with responsibility for the orphans' welfare.
2:220.source: Ibn Kathir on 2:220; Ibn Jarir, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i, report of Ibn 'Abbas

5:101.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites repeated questions about whether Hajj was required every year. The Prophet ﷺ answered that saying yes would have made it obligatory. This illustrates how pressing for additional rulings during revelation could impose burdens not originally required.
5:101.source: Ibn Kathir on 5:101; Imam Ahmad, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, report of 'Ali

2:143.occasion: After the prayer direction changed, Muslims worried about those who had died praying toward Jerusalem. ‘Allah would never waste your faith’ reassures them that those earlier prayers remained valid—not that the new direction invalidated past obedience.
2:143.source: Ibn Kathir on 2:143; Al-Bukhari and Muslim

2:187.occasion: Early in Ramadan fasting, falling asleep ended the night's permission to eat, even before a meal. Qays bin Sirmah slept while awaiting food and collapsed the next day. This verse lifted that restriction, allowing eating and drinking until dawn.
2:187.source: Ibn Kathir on 2:187, report of Al-Bara' bin 'Azib

4:19.occasion: A dead man's male relatives once claimed control over his widow: they could marry her, marry her to someone else, or prevent her remarriage. ‘Inherit women’ prohibits this control over a person, not merely taking her property.
4:19.source: Ibn Kathir on 4:19; Al-Bukhari, report of Ibn 'Abbas

62:11.occasion: A trading caravan arrived in Madinah during the Friday sermon. People left to meet it, leaving only twelve men with the Prophet ﷺ. ‘Standing’ describes him still delivering the sermon—not an ordinary gathering interrupted by shopping.
62:11.source: Ibn Kathir on 62:11; Imam Ahmad and the Two Sahihs, report of Jabir

2:158.occasion: Some Ansar hesitated to walk between Safa and Marwah because of their former worship of Manat. Aishah explained that ‘no sin’ removes that hesitation; it does not mean the rite may be omitted.
2:158.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:170.occasion: It was revealed about a group of Jews whom the Messenger of Allah called to Islam. They refused, saying they would rather follow what they had found their forefathers practicing.
2:170.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:189.occasion: People asked the Messenger of Allah about the crescent moons, so the verse was revealed explaining that they are time-markers for the worship, the waiting periods of women, and the Hajj of mankind. The remainder of the verse was revealed because the Ansar used to enter their houses from the back rather than through the front doors when returning from a journey, considering this a form of piety.
2:189.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:195.occasion: It was revealed concerning the Ansar who, after Islam became strong and victorious, privately resolved among themselves to return to their long-neglected estates, families, and properties and to give up Jihad. The verse clarified that abandoning the cause of Allah, not fighting, is the true self-destruction.
2:195.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:196.occasion: Ka'b bin 'Ujrah was brought to the Prophet while in Ihram with lice falling in great numbers over his face. The Prophet directed him to shave his head and pay a ransom by fasting three days, feeding six poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep. Ka'b said this ruling was revealed regarding his own case in particular, though it then applied to everyone in general.
2:196.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:207.occasion: It was revealed about Suhayb bin Sinan ar-Rumi. When he became a Muslim in Makkah and wished to emigrate, the Quraysh would not let him leave with his wealth, so he gave up all his property to them and chose to migrate for the sake of Allah.
2:207.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:223.occasion: The Jews used to claim that if a man approached his wife from behind, in the vagina, the resulting child would be born cross-eyed. After some of the Ansar also asked the Prophet about this, the verse was revealed declaring that wives are a tilth and that a man may approach his wife as he wishes so long as it is in the proper place.
2:223.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:229.occasion: Ibn Jarir reported that it was revealed concerning Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas and his wife, in the context of khul', where the wife sought release from the marriage by returning what she had been given.
2:229.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:232.occasion: It was revealed about Ma'qil bin Yasar al-Muzani. His sister had been divorced by her husband, and after her waiting period ended the husband sought to remarry her and she was willing, but Ma'qil refused to allow it. The verse forbade guardians from preventing women from returning to their former husbands in such a case.
2:232.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:267.occasion: It was revealed about some of the Ansar who, when the date harvest came, would hang branches of dates in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah for the poor emigrants to eat, but some of them would mix in inferior, poor-quality dates among the good ones.
2:267.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:278.occasion: It was revealed concerning outstanding usurious dealings left over from the time of Jahiliyyah between Banu 'Amr bin 'Umayr of the tribe of Thaqif and Banu al-Mughirah of Makhzum. When both tribes embraced Islam, a dispute arose over paying the accumulated interest, the matter was referred to the Messenger of Allah, and the verse was revealed forbidding the taking of the remaining riba.
2:278.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

2:285.occasion: When Ayah 2:284 was revealed ("Whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it"), the Companions were deeply shaken, wept, and fell to their knees before the Prophet ﷺ, saying they could bear prayer, fasting, and charity, but could not control involuntary thoughts crossing their hearts. The Prophet ﷺ told them: "Do not say like the People of the Book: 'We hear and disobey.' Rather say: 'We hear and obey; forgive us our Lord, and to You is the return.'" When they submitted and their tongues humbled to it, Allah revealed 2:285 praising their submission, followed immediately by 2:286 lifting the burden: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear..."

2:286.occasion: Revealed directly following the Companions' submission in 2:285. After they humbled their hearts and pleaded: "We hear and we obey; grant us Your forgiveness, our Lord", Allah revealed this verse relieving their distress, confirming that involuntary passing thoughts will not be penalized, and guaranteeing that no soul is burdened beyond its capacity.

3:13.occasion: After Allah granted the Muslims victory at Badr and the Prophet (peace be upon him) returned to Al-Madinah, he gathered the Jews in the marketplace of Bani Qaynuqa' and warned them. This passage was addressed to them, pointing to the two armies that met at Badr as a sign that Allah would make His religion prevail.
3:13.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:65.occasion: The Christians of Najran and the Jewish rabbis disputed before the Prophet (peace be upon him), the Jews claiming that Ibrahim was a Jew and the Christians claiming he was a Christian. This verse was revealed in response, pointing out that the Tawrah and Injil were sent down only after his time.
3:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:77.occasion: Al-Ash'ath bin Qays had a dispute with a Jewish man over a piece of land; the Jew denied his right and Al-Ash'ath had no evidence. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) called on the Jew to swear an oath, Al-Ash'ath feared he would swear falsely and seize the land, and this verse was revealed concerning that.
3:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:90.occasion: Some people embraced Islam, then disbelieved, then became Muslims again, and then reverted once more. They sent word inquiring about their case and the matter was put to the Prophet (peace be upon him), so this verse was revealed about those who increase in disbelief.
3:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:103.occasion: This verse about Allah uniting the hearts of the believers was revealed concerning the Aws and Khazraj, who had been bitter enemies engaged in long wars during the time of Jahiliyyah, until Allah joined their hearts through Islam and made them brothers.
3:103.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:113.occasion: These verses were revealed about the People of the Scripture who embraced Islam, such as 'Abdullah bin Salam, Asad bin 'Ubayd, Tha'labah bin Sa'yah and Usayd bin Sa'yah, distinguishing them from those of the People of the Book who were rebuked earlier.
3:113.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:122.occasion: This verse about the two parties who were about to lose heart was revealed concerning the two Muslim clans Bani Harithah and Bani Salamah at the battle of Uhud, of whom Allah said that He was their Protector.
3:122.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:128.occasion: This verse was revealed regarding the Prophet (peace be upon him) invoking Allah against certain disbelievers of Quraysh during the prayer (such as Al-Harith bin Hisham, Suhayl bin 'Amr and Safwan bin Umayyah), and after he was wounded at Uhud and said, 'How can a people achieve success after having injured their Prophet?' He was told the decision belonged to Allah alone.
3:128.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:144.occasion: During the battle of Uhud a rumor spread that the Prophet (peace be upon him) had been killed, which weakened the resolve of some Muslims who stopped fighting. This verse was revealed reminding them that Muhammad is only a Messenger and that the death or killing of the Messenger must not turn them back from their religion.
3:144.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:161.occasion: A red cloak went missing from the spoils of war at Badr, and some people suggested the Prophet (peace be upon him) might have taken it. This verse was revealed to clear him of any treachery regarding the booty.
3:161.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:165.occasion: When the Muslims suffered the loss of seventy men at Uhud, a year after Badr, this verse was revealed in connection with their having accepted ransom from the captives of Badr; the calamity was a consequence of their own choices.
3:165.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:168.occasion: This verse, describing those who stayed behind and said of their slain brethren that they would not have been killed had they listened, was revealed concerning 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, the chief of the hypocrites.
3:168.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:169.occasion: These verses about the martyrs being alive with their Lord were revealed concerning those killed at Uhud. Allah placed their souls in green birds wandering in Paradise, and when they wished their brethren could know their state, Allah said He would convey the news to them.
3:169.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:173.occasion: This verse was revealed concerning the believers who, after Uhud, were told that the enemy had gathered against them in order to frighten them, yet it only increased their faith and they said, 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs' (during the expedition to Hamra' Al-Asad).
3:173.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:181.occasion: When the verse calling for a goodly loan to Allah (2:245) was revealed, the Jews said, 'Has Allah become poor that He asks His servants for a loan?' This verse was revealed in response to their statement that Allah is poor and they are rich.
3:181.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

3:186.occasion: Before the battle of Badr, the Prophet (peace be upon him) passed a gathering that included 'Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who spoke offensively, and the Muslims, idolaters and Jews nearly came to blows. Allah commanded the believers to be patient and forbearing in the face of the abuse they would hear from the People of the Scripture and the idolaters.
3:186.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:3.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from al-Bukhari that 'A'ishah said a man was the guardian of a female orphan and married her although he had no desire for her, mixing her wealth with his and withholding her share. This verse was revealed concerning his case, forbidding guardians from marrying their orphan wards unless they treated them justly and gave a fair dowry.
4:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:7.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Jabir that Umm Kujjah came to the Messenger of Allah saying she had two daughters whose father had died and who owned nothing, after which this verse on inheritance shares for men and women was revealed.
4:7.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Jabir that the wife of Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' came to the Prophet about her two daughters by Sa'd, who was martyred at Uhud, complaining that their uncle had taken all their inheritance. The verse of inheritance was then revealed, and the Prophet ordered two-thirds for the daughters, an eighth for their mother, and the rest for the uncle.
4:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:24.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that at Awtas the Muslims captured women who were already married and were reluctant to have relations with them. They asked the Prophet, and this verse permitting captives whom their right hands possessed was revealed.
4:24.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:43.occasion: Ibn Kathir records that Sa'd narrated this verse was revealed after an Ansari man hosted a meal where the guests drank until intoxicated and boasted, and a man struck Sa'd's nose with a camel bone. He also cites 'Ali that 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf served wine at a meal, and when the intoxicated man led the prayer he misrecited Surat al-Kafirun, so the verse forbidding prayer while drunk was revealed.
4:43.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:58.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports it is well known, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj and 'Umar, that this verse on rendering back trusts was revealed concerning 'Uthman bin Talhah, from whom the Prophet took the key of the Ka'bah on the day Makkah was conquered; the Prophet then recited the verse and returned the key to him.
4:58.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:59.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites al-Bukhari from Ibn 'Abbas that this verse commanding obedience to those in authority was revealed about 'Abdullah bin Hudhafah bin Qays, whom the Messenger of Allah had sent in command of a military expedition.
4:59.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:65.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from al-Bukhari that az-Zubayr disputed with an Ansari man over irrigation water; when the Prophet judged in az-Zubayr's favor the Ansari accused him of partiality because az-Zubayr was his relative. Az-Zubayr said he believed this verse, swearing none truly believe until they accept the Prophet's judgment, was revealed concerning that case.
4:65.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:69.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites the report of Sa'id bin Jubayr that an Ansari man came to the Prophet grieving that, although he loved sitting with him, in the Hereafter the Prophet would be raised with the Prophets and he feared he would not see him. Jibril then brought this verse promising the obedient the company of the Prophets, and the Prophet sent the man the good news.
4:69.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:77.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf and companions came to the Prophet in Makkah saying they had been mighty as idolaters but became weak after believing, and he told them he was commanded to pardon and not to fight. After the move to al-Madinah they were commanded to fight, yet some held back, so this verse was revealed about those told to restrain their hands.
4:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:83.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Muslim that when 'Umar heard a rumor circulating that the Messenger of Allah had divorced his wives, he went and asked the Prophet directly, who said he had not, after which 'Umar proclaimed the truth and this verse on properly investigating reports of safety or fear was revealed.
4:83.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:88.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Zayd bin Thabit that when the Messenger marched toward Uhud some who set out turned back to al-Madinah, and the Companions split into two groups over them, one saying they should be killed and the other objecting. This verse rebuking their division over the hypocrites was then revealed.
4:88.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:97.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that some men in Makkah claimed Islam yet went out with the idolaters and were killed among them at Badr; this verse was revealed about those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves by failing to emigrate.
4:97.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

4:127.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites al-Bukhari that 'A'ishah explained this verse was revealed about the guardian of a female orphan whose wealth was joined to his, who desired to marry her himself for gain without giving her a fair dowry, or else refused to let her marry anyone else.
4:127.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Zayd bin Aslam that at Al-Hudaybiyyah, after the idolators had prevented the Muslims from visiting the House, some idolators passed by from the east intending 'Umrah. The Companions said, 'Let us prevent these just as their fellows prevented us,' so Allah revealed the warning not to let hatred for a people lead them to transgression.
5:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir mentions that Muhammad bin Ishaq, Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said this was revealed about Banu An-Nadir, who plotted to drop a stone on the Prophet's head when he came to them seeking help to pay blood money. Allah informed His Prophet of the plot and he returned safely to Al-Madinah, and this verse about Allah withholding their hands was sent down.
5:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:41.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Umar that two Jews, a man and a woman, committed adultery, and the Jews came to the Prophet seeking his judgment, having concealed the verse of stoning in the Tawrah, intending to follow him only if he ruled for flogging. The Prophet had the verse of stoning uncovered and ordered the two to be stoned, and these verses were revealed about them.
5:41.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:42.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that these verses concerned the blood money dispute between Bani An-Nadir and Bani Qurayzah, where the dead of An-Nadir received full blood money while Qurayzah received only half. They referred the matter to the Messenger of Allah, who made the blood money equal for both groups, and these verses were sent down.
5:42.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:49.occasion: Ibn Kathir cites Muhammad bin Ishaq from Ibn 'Abbas that Jewish chiefs including Ka'b bin Asad, Ibn Saluba, 'Abdullah bin Surya and Shas bin Qays came to the Prophet offering to believe in him if he ruled in their favor in a dispute with their own people, hoping to misguide him from his religion. The Prophet refused, and these verses were revealed about them.
5:49.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

5:87.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that this was revealed about some Companions who resolved to renounce worldly desires, abandon women and travel the land like monks. When the Prophet heard, he summoned them and declared that he himself fasts and breaks his fast, prays and sleeps, and marries women, and that whoever turns away from his Sunnah is not of him.
5:87.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:93.occasion: Ikrimah and Qatadah stated that the verse condemning whoever invents a lie against Allah or falsely claims 'I have received inspiration' was revealed concerning Musaylimah the Liar, who falsely claimed to receive revelation.
6:93.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:108.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that the disbelievers said to the Prophet, 'You will stop insulting our gods, or we will insult your Lord.' So Allah forbade the believers from insulting the idols of the idolaters, lest they retaliate by insulting Allah out of ignorance. Qatadah related the same, that Muslims used to insult the idols and the disbelievers responded by insulting Allah.
6:108.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

6:141.occasion: Ibn Jurayj reported that the command 'waste not by extravagance' was revealed concerning Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, who, upon harvesting his date palms, resolved to feed everyone who came to him that day until he was left with no dates by evening.
6:141.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

7:31.occasion: This verse was revealed concerning the idolaters who used to perform Tawaf around the Sacred House while naked, both men and women. Allah commanded them to take their adornment, meaning to wear proper clothes that cover the body, at every place of prayer.
7:31.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:1.occasion: At Badr the Muslims disputed over the war spoils: those who had collected them, those who had pursued the enemy, and those who had guarded the Prophet each claimed a greater right. The verse was revealed taking the Anfal away from their dispute and assigning them to Allah and the Messenger, who then divided them equally among the Muslims.
8:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:19.occasion: At Badr Abu Jahl prayed, asking Allah to destroy whichever of the two armies had severed the ties of kinship and brought what was not recognized. This verse was revealed in response, telling the disbelievers that the judgement they had sought had now come to them.
8:19.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:36.occasion: After their defeat at Badr, leading men of Quraysh who had lost relatives went to Abu Sufyan and those whose wealth was in the caravan, urging them to spend that wealth to finance fighting against the Prophet. This verse was revealed about their spending to hinder others from the path of Allah.
8:36.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:47.occasion: When the Quraysh set out toward Badr, Abu Jahl refused to turn back even after the caravan was safe, vowing to reach the wells of Badr to slaughter camels, drink, and have singing-girls perform so the Arabs would always speak of them. They marched out boastfully and to be seen of men, and this verse was revealed about them.
8:47.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:67.occasion: After Badr the Prophet consulted the Companions about the captives. Umar urged that they be executed, while Abu Bakr advised pardoning them in return for ransom; the Prophet accepted ransom. These verses were then revealed concerning the taking of captives and the ransom that was taken.
8:67.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

8:70.occasion: Al-Abbas, the Prophet's uncle, was captured at Badr and ransomed himself and his nephews, saying he had been left poor. This verse was revealed promising the captives that if Allah knew any good in their hearts He would give them better than what had been taken; Al-Abbas later said Allah replaced his loss many times over.
8:70.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:19.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that this passage was revealed concerning Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Muttalib. When he was taken captive at the battle of Badr and was reproached for his disbelief, he boasted that the idolaters used to maintain Al-Masjid Al-Haram, provide water for the pilgrims, and free the indebted. Allah then revealed that such deeds, done in a state of Shirk, are not equal to faith and Jihad.
9:19.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:49.occasion: This was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qays, a chief of Banu Salimah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) invited him to march to Tabuk against the Romans, he asked to be excused, claiming that he feared he could not restrain himself if he saw the Roman women, and asking not to be put to trial. Allah declared that he had already fallen into trial.
9:49.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:74.occasion: This was revealed about Al-Julas bin Suwayd, one of the hypocrites who lagged behind. He said that if Muhammad (peace be upon him) was telling the truth, they were worse than donkeys. His stepson Umayr bin Sa'd reported this to the Prophet, and Al-Julas swore by Allah that he had said nothing of the sort, so this verse was sent down. It is also said the verse refers to the hypocrites who plotted to throw the Prophet from the mountain pass at Tabuk.
9:74.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:79.occasion: This was revealed when the Prophet (peace be upon him) called the people to give charity. Abdur-Rahman bin Awf gave a large amount and the hypocrites accused him of showing off, while Abu Aqil brought only a small measure (a Sa') of dates and they mocked him, saying Allah had no need of it. Allah rebuked those who defamed both the generous and the poor giver.
9:79.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:84.occasion: Ibn Umar reported that when Abdullah bin Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, died, his son asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) for his shirt as a shroud and asked him to pray the funeral prayer over him. The Prophet did so despite Umar's objection. Afterwards this verse was revealed forbidding the Prophet from ever praying over a hypocrite who dies or standing at his grave.
9:84.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:102.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that this was revealed about Abu Lubabah and a group with him who stayed behind from the battle of Tabuk. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) returned, they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and refused to be untied by anyone but him. When the verse was revealed, the Prophet untied them and pardoned them.
9:102.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:107.occasion: These verses were revealed about Masjid Ad-Dirar, which a group of hypocrites built next to Masjid Quba at the instigation of Abu Amir Ar-Rahib, who had fled to the Romans to seek their aid against the Prophet (peace be upon him). They intended it to harm the believers, spread disbelief, divide them, and serve as an outpost for Abu Amir, then invited the Prophet to pray in it. Allah forbade him, and on his return from Tabuk he ordered it demolished.
9:107.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

9:118.occasion: Ka'b bin Malik reported that this was revealed about himself and his two companions, Murarah bin Ar-Rabi' and Hilal bin Umayyah, who stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition without an excuse. Unlike the hypocrites, they told the Prophet (peace be upon him) the truth. He deferred their case and ordered the Muslims to shun them for fifty nights, until the earth was straitened for them, after which Allah revealed the acceptance of their repentance.
9:118.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

10:2.occasion: Ad-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas that when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a Messenger, most of the Arabs denied him and his message, saying that Allah is greater than to send a human Messenger like Muhammad. So Allah revealed this verse rebuking their astonishment that revelation was sent to a man from among themselves.
10:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

10:59.occasion: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said this verse was revealed to criticize the idolators for what they used to declare lawful and unlawful on their own, such as the Bahirah, Sa'ibah and Wasilah (categories of camels they consecrated and forbade), affirming that none can make things lawful or unlawful except Allah.
10:59.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

11:5.occasion: Ibn Abbas explained that some people felt ashamed to be uncovered toward the sky, whether during intimacy with their wives or while relieving themselves in the open, fearing exposure to the heavens. This verse was revealed concerning them, affirming that Allah knows what they conceal and reveal.
11:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

11:114.occasion: A man kissed a woman who was not lawful to him and then came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and told him what he had done. This verse, commanding prayer at the two ends of the day and stating that good deeds remove evil deeds, was then revealed. When the man asked if it was only for him, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said it was for all of his followers.
11:114.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

13:8.occasion: These verses (13:8-11) were revealed concerning Arbad bin Qays and 'Amir bin At-Tufayl, who came to the Prophet in Al-Madinah plotting to kill him. 'Amir distracted the Prophet so Arbad could strike him with his sword, but Arbad's hand froze on the hilt and he could not draw it. As they departed, Allah struck Arbad dead with a thunderbolt of lightning, while 'Amir died of a sudden ulcer.
13:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

15:91.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Abbas that as the Hajj season approached, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah gathered a group of Quraysh and urged them to agree on one verdict about the Prophet (peace be upon him) before the Arab delegations arrived. After rejecting calling him a soothsayer, madman, or poet, they settled on branding him a sorcerer, and Allah revealed this concerning them.
15:91.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

16:41.occasion: Ibn Kathir notes that this verse may have been revealed concerning those who emigrated for Allah's sake to Ethiopia after being severely persecuted by their own people in Makkah, among the most prominent being Uthman bin Affan with his wife Ruqayyah, Jafar bin Abi Talib, and Abu Salamah bin Abdul-Asad, in a group of almost eighty believing men and women.
16:41.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

16:43.occasion: Reported from Ibn Abbas: when Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a Messenger, some of the Arabs rejected him and said that Allah was too great to send a human being as a Messenger. In response Allah revealed that He had only ever sent men as Messengers before him, and told the deniers to ask the People of the earlier Scriptures whether their Prophets had been humans or angels.
16:43.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

16:90.occasion: Reported from Ibn Abbas: while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was sitting with Uthman bin Maz'un, a messenger from Allah (the angel) came to him and conveyed this verse, 'Verily, Allah orders justice and kindness.' When Uthman heard it, faith became firmly established in his heart and he began to love the Prophet (peace be upon him).
16:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

16:126.occasion: Reported from Ibn Zayd: the Muslims had been commanded to forgive the idolators; then some men who had become strong and powerful after embracing Islam asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) for permission to take revenge on the idolators. This verse permitting equal retaliation was then revealed, and was later abrogated by the command to engage in Jihad.
16:126.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:59.occasion: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) to turn the hill of As-Safa into gold and to remove the mountains so they could farm the land. He was offered the choice of granting their demand, after which they would be destroyed if they still disbelieved, or of giving them more time; he chose to give them respite, and this verse was revealed.
17:59.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:76.occasion: This was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Quraysh when they sought to drive the Prophet (peace be upon him) out of Makkah, warning them that had they expelled him they themselves would not have remained there long afterward.
17:76.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

17:85.occasion: The Quraysh sent an inquiry to the Jewish rabbis in Madinah asking for a test of Muhammad's prophethood. The rabbis told them: "Ask him about three things: the young men who disappeared in ancient times (the Sleepers of the Cave), the great traveler who reached the ends of the earth (Dhul-Qarnayn), and what the Spirit (ar-Ruh) is." When they asked the Prophet ﷺ about the Spirit, he remained silent until Jibril descended with this revelation: "And they ask you concerning the Spirit. Say: 'The Spirit is of the affair of my Lord, and of knowledge you have been given but a little.'"

17:90.occasion: The leaders of the Quraysh gathered behind the Kabah and summoned the Prophet (peace be upon him), offering him wealth, leadership, or kingship to abandon his message, then demanding that he produce specific signs such as causing a spring to gush forth, growing gardens, making the sky fall in pieces, or ascending to heaven and bringing down a book they could read. These verses were revealed concerning their demands.
17:90.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

18:23.occasion: When the Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ the three questions about the Sleepers of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, the Prophet ﷺ eagerly said: "I will tell you tomorrow," without adding "in sha Allah" (if Allah wills). Revelation was paused for fifteen days, causing the Prophet great grief and prompting the pagans to mock him, until Surah al-Kahf was revealed with the divine admonition: "And never say of anything, 'I will do that tomorrow,' without adding, 'If Allah wills.'"

18:28.occasion: The nobles of Quraysh asked the Prophet to sit with them alone and to send away his poor and weak Companions, such as Bilal, 'Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab and Ibn Mas'ud, so they would not be offended by their presence. Allah forbade him from driving them away and commanded him to remain patiently in the company of those who call upon their Lord.
18:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

18:32.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that the parable of the two men, one of whom owned two gardens, was revealed concerning Al-'As bin Wa'il.
18:32.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

19:77.occasion: Khabbab bin Al-Aratt, a blacksmith, came to collect a debt from Al-'As bin Wa'il. Al-'As refused to pay unless Khabbab disbelieved in Muhammad, and mockingly claimed that when he was resurrected he would be given wealth and children and would repay him then. These verses were revealed in response.
19:77.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:3.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from As-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, that this verse was revealed concerning An-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and that Ibn Jurayj held the same view.
22:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:11.occasion: Al-Bukhari recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that this was revealed about people who would come to Al-Madinah to declare their Islam: if their wives bore sons and their mares foaled they would say it was a good religion, but if not, they would say it was a bad religion and turn away.
22:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:19.occasion: Recorded in the Two Sahihs, Abu Dharr swore that this verse was revealed concerning the men who came forward for single combat at the Battle of Badr: Hamzah, 'Ali and 'Ubaydah on one side, and 'Utbah, Shaybah and Al-Walid on the other.
22:19.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:25.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that the warning against wrongdoing in the Sacred Precinct was revealed concerning 'Abdullah bin Unays, who killed an Ansari companion after a quarrel over lineage, then apostatized and fled to Makkah.
22:25.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

22:39.occasion: Ibn 'Abbas reported that when the Prophet was driven out of Makkah, Abu Bakr said the people were doomed; then Allah revealed this verse giving permission to fight, and Abu Bakr knew there would be fighting. Ibn 'Abbas said it was the first verse revealed concerning fighting.
22:39.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

23:76.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn 'Abbas that Abu Sufyan came to the Messenger of Allah and, appealing to him by Allah and by the ties of kinship between them, complained that the Quraysh had been reduced to eating camel hair and blood during the famine. Allah then revealed this verse, 'And indeed We seized them with punishment, but they humbled not themselves to their Lord.'
23:76.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:6.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that the verses of Li'an (mutual cursing) were revealed concerning Hilal bin Umayyah, who came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) accusing his wife of adultery with Sharik bin Sahma' but could not produce four witnesses. When he insisted he was truthful and feared the punishment for slander, Allah revealed the procedure of Li'an as a way out for him.
24:6.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:11.occasion: Revealed during the Incident of the Slander (al-Ifk) on the return from the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq. Aishah was accidentally left behind when her caravan departed while she looked for her lost necklace. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal escorted her back to Madinah on his camel. Abdullah ibn Ubayy, chief of the hypocrites, seized on this to circulate a malicious lie impugning her chastity, causing severe distress to the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr for a month until Allah directly vindicated her innocence in these verses.

24:22.occasion: This verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, who had sworn that he would never again spend on his poor relative Mistah bin Uthathah after Mistah took part in the slander against Aishah. When the verse was revealed, Abu Bakr resumed his support of Mistah, saying he loved that Allah should forgive him.
24:22.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:23.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that this warning against those who accuse chaste, believing women was revealed primarily concerning Aishah bint Abi Bakr, the mother of the believers, in the aftermath of the slander made against her.
24:23.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:31.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Muqatil bin Hayyan that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that Asma' bint Murshidah, in her home among Banu Harithah, saw women coming in without proper covering so that their anklets, chests and forelocks were exposed, and she remarked how ugly this was; then Allah revealed the command for believing women to lower their gaze and cover themselves.
24:31.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:33.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that the prohibition against forcing slave-girls into prostitution was revealed concerning Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, who used to compel his slave-girls (such as Musaykah and Mu'adhah) to commit immorality so that he could take their earnings, even though they wished to remain chaste.
24:33.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

24:37.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Umar that this verse, describing men whom neither trade nor business diverts from the remembrance of Allah, was revealed concerning people who, when the call to prayer was given while they were in the marketplace, would close their shops and hasten to the mosque.
24:37.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

25:68.occasion: Ibn 'Abbas related that some of the idolaters who had killed and committed unlawful sexual acts a great deal came to the Prophet and said that what he called people to was good, if only there were a way to expiate what they had done. This verse, together with 39:53, was then revealed.
25:68.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

28:52.occasion: Sa'id bin Jubayr reported that these verses were revealed concerning a delegation of about seventy priests sent by An-Najashi (the Negus of Ethiopia). When they came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, he recited Surah Ya Sin to them; they wept and embraced Islam, and these verses about those who already believed before the Qur'an were revealed concerning them.
28:52.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

28:56.occasion: Recorded in the Two Sahihs as having been revealed concerning Abu Talib, the paternal uncle of the Prophet, peace be upon him, who protected and loved him out of kinship. As Abu Talib lay dying, the Prophet urged him to say La ilaha illallah, but Abu Jahl and 'Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah pressed him to remain on the religion of 'Abdul-Muttalib, and he died refusing to make the declaration.
28:56.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

29:8.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that several verses were revealed concerning him. His mother vowed that she would neither eat nor drink until he abandoned Islam, and when food was offered to her she refused it; so this verse was revealed, enjoining kindness to parents yet forbidding obedience to them when they call to associating partners with Allah.
29:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

30:1.occasion: These verses were revealed when the Persians had defeated the Romans. The idolaters of Makkah favored the Persians, who were idol worshippers, while the Muslims favored the Romans because they were People of the Book. When the verses foretold that the Romans would be victorious within a few years, Abu Bakr proclaimed this in Makkah and made a wager with the idolaters over the outcome, which the Romans later fulfilled.
30:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

30:28.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that the idolaters used to say in their Talbiyah, declaring that Allah had no partner except a partner whom He owned along with whatever that partner owned. Allah then revealed this verse setting forth the parable that they would not accept their own servants as equal partners in their wealth, so how could they ascribe partners to Allah.
30:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

31:15.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports, on the authority of Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas, that this verse was revealed concerning him. He was devoted to his mother, but when he became Muslim she refused to eat or drink, threatening to starve herself to death so that he would abandon his religion. Sa'd remained firm and told her that he would not give up his faith for anything, so eventually she ate.
31:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

32:18.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from 'Ata' bin Yasar, As-Suddi and others that this verse, contrasting the believer with the rebellious, was revealed concerning 'Ali bin Abi Talib and 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'it.
32:18.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:4.occasion: Revealed concerning Zayd bin Harithah, the freed servant whom the Prophet had adopted before prophethood and who used to be called Zayd bin Muhammad. Allah ended this practice, declaring that adopted sons are not real sons and should be named after their own fathers.
33:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:28.occasion: Revealed when the Prophet's wives asked him to increase their provision and maintenance. Allah commanded him to offer them the choice between the life of this world, in which case he would release them handsomely, or remaining with him desiring Allah, His Messenger and the Hereafter.
33:28.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:35.occasion: Revealed after Umm Salamah asked the Prophet why women were not mentioned in the Qur'an as men were; he then announced this verse from the Minbar naming believing men and women together.
33:35.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:36.occasion: Reported to have been revealed concerning a young Ansari woman whom the Prophet asked in marriage on behalf of Julaybib; when her mother objected, the girl submitted to the command of the Messenger of Allah, saying she would not refuse what he had decreed.
33:36.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:37.occasion: Revealed concerning the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh after his adopted son Zayd bin Harithah had divorced her, so that it would no longer be considered difficult for believers to marry the former wives of their adopted sons.
33:37.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

33:50.occasion: The portion concerning a believing woman who offers herself to the Prophet was connected by Aisha to Khawlah bint Hakim, who offered herself in marriage to the Prophet.
33:50.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

36:8.occasion: Ikrimah reported that Abu Jahl said, 'If I see Muhammad, I will do such and such,' threatening the Prophet. Then Allah revealed the verses, 'Verily, We have put on their necks iron collars... so that they cannot see.' Afterwards, when people pointed out the Prophet to him, Abu Jahl would say, 'Where is he?' and was unable to see him.
36:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

36:78.occasion: Ubayy bin Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah with a dry, crumbling bone and said, 'O Muhammad! Are you claiming that Allah will resurrect this?' The Prophet replied that Allah would cause him to die, then resurrect him and gather him into the Fire. It is also reported that Al-'As bin Wa'il did the same with a decayed bone. Then these verses at the end of Surah Ya-Sin were revealed: 'Does not man see that We have created him from a Nutfah...' to the end of the surah.
36:78.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

38:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that when Abu Talib fell ill, leaders of the Quraysh, including Abu Jahl, came to him and complained that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was insulting their gods. The Prophet was summoned and asked them to accept a single statement, 'La ilaha illallah,' by which the Arabs and non-Arabs would submit to them. They stood up in agitation and said this was a curious thing, and this passage (verses 4 through 8) was then revealed.
38:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

39:17.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports, on the authority of 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam from his father, that the verse about those who avoid worshipping false gods (At-Taghut) and turn to Allah was revealed concerning Zayd bin 'Amr bin Nufayl, Abu Dharr, and Salman Al-Farisi. He adds that the correct view is that it includes them and all others who shunned idols and turned to the worship of the Most Merciful.
39:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

39:53.occasion: Al-Bukhari recorded from Ibn 'Abbas that some idolators who had killed many people and committed much fornication came to the Prophet and said that what he was calling them to was good, if only he could tell them there was an expiation for what they had done. Then this verse, along with the verses of Surah Al-Furqan (25:68-70), was revealed.
39:53.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

39:64.occasion: Ibn Kathir, citing Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn 'Abbas, states that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that the idolators, in their ignorance, called the Messenger of Allah to worship their gods, proposing that they would then worship his God along with him; so these words were revealed.
39:64.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

43:57.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates that after the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited that they and what they worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell, 'Abdullah bin Az-Zab'ari argued contentiously that the Christians worship 'Isa, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and Quraysh worship the angels, so would they all be in the Fire. The Quraysh were delighted and clamored at this argument, and this verse was revealed concerning their disputatious objection to the mention of the son of Maryam.
43:57.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

44:15.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that a man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and asked him to pray for rain for the tribe of Mudar, who were dying. The Prophet prayed and rain was sent to them, whereupon the verse 'Verily, We shall remove the torment for a while; verily, you will revert' was revealed.
44:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

46:15.occasion: This verse enjoining kindness to parents was revealed concerning Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas (RA), whose mother swore she would neither eat nor drink until he renounced his faith, abstaining so stubbornly that they had to force her mouth open with a stick.
46:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

47:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir notes that this verse, with its ruling on captives and freeing them by grace or ransom, appears to have been revealed after the battle of Badr, when Allah reproached the believers for sparing many of the enemy and holding too many captives in order to take ransom from them.
47:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

47:13.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Abbas that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) left Makkah during the Hijrah and reached the cave, he looked back toward Makkah and said it was the most beloved of Allah's lands to Allah and to him, and that he would never have left it had its people not driven him out. Allah then revealed this verse about the destruction of towns mightier than the town that expelled him.
47:13.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:1.occasion: Revealed on the return journey from the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH). The Companions were initially crestfallen and grieved by what seemed to be unfavorable terms agreed upon with the Quraysh (such as returning without performing Umrah that year). Umar ibn al-Khattab asked: "Is this really a victory, O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet ﷺ replied: "Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is a victory!" The treaty allowed peaceful interaction, leading to more people accepting Islam over the next two years than in the entire prior history of Islam.

48:11.occasion: This was revealed concerning the bedouins who lagged behind and did not set out with the Prophet for Al-Hudaybiyyah, preferring their possessions and families. They asked the Prophet to seek forgiveness for them, saying with their tongues what was not in their hearts.
48:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:15.occasion: This was revealed concerning those bedouins who had lagged behind at Al-Hudaybiyyah and then asked to accompany the Muslims to take the spoils of Khaybar. Allah commanded His Messenger to refuse them, since the spoils of Khaybar had been promised to those who were present at Al-Hudaybiyyah.
48:15.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:24.occasion: Anas bin Malik reported that on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah about eighty armed men came down from Mount At-Tan'im to ambush the Messenger of Allah; he invoked Allah against them and they were captured, then he pardoned them, and this verse was revealed concerning that incident.
48:24.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:26.occasion: This was revealed concerning the pride and haughtiness the disbelievers showed during the treaty negotiations at Al-Hudaybiyyah, when they refused to allow the words 'In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful' and 'Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah' to be written in the treaty document.
48:26.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

48:27.occasion: This was revealed concerning the true dream-vision Allah showed the Prophet of entering Makkah and performing Tawaf, which he told his Companions in Al-Madinah. When the Hudaybiyyah treaty forced them to return without entering Makkah that year, some Companions, including 'Umar, questioned this, and the verse confirmed the vision would be fulfilled.
48:27.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:2.occasion: It was stated that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Umar. When a delegation from Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (peace be upon him), the two of them differed over whom to recommend as its leader and raised their voices in his presence until their dispute grew loud, whereupon this verse was revealed.
49:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:4.occasion: It was reported, according to more than one source, that this verse was revealed concerning Al-Aqra bin Habis At-Tamimi, who came and called out to the Prophet (peace be upon him) from behind his dwellings, repeatedly saying, 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!'
49:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:11.occasion: Abu Jabirah bin Ad-Dahhak said this verse was revealed concerning Banu Salamah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) came to Madinah, every man among them had two or three nicknames, and when he called a man by one of them people would say he disliked that name, so the prohibition against insulting one another by nicknames was revealed.
49:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

49:17.occasion: Ibn Abbas related that Banu Asad came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we embraced Islam, and the Arabs fought you while we did not fight you,' counting their Islam as a favor to him. This verse was then revealed.
49:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

52:30.occasion: Ibn Abbas reported that when the Quraysh gathered in their assembly hall (Dar An-Nadwah) to plot against the Prophet (peace be upon him), one of them proposed imprisoning him in chains and waiting for death to overtake him as it had earlier poets such as Zuhayr and An-Nabighah, claiming he was merely a poet like them. In response Allah revealed, 'Or do they say: A poet! We await for him some calamity by time!'
52:30.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

54:49.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Abu Hurairah that the idolaters of the Quraysh came to the Messenger of Allah arguing with him and disputing the divine decree (Qadar). In response this verse, affirming that Allah created all things with measure, was revealed.
54:49.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

57:27.occasion: Ibn Abbas related that after 'Isa, kings altered the Tawrah and Injil while some believers still recited the originals. Persecuted and threatened with death unless they abandoned the true scriptures, these believers withdrew from society, some building towers, some wandering the land, and some constructing hermitages in deserts where they could worship in seclusion. Ibn Kathir reports that the portion of this verse about the monasticism people invented for themselves was revealed concerning them.
57:27.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

58:1.occasion: Khawlah bint Tha'labah came to the Prophet ﷺ weeping and complaining after her elderly husband, Aws ibn al-Samit, pronounced 'zihar' upon her (a pre-Islamic pagan custom where a man declared his wife as unlawful to him as his mother's back, leaving her neither married nor free to remarry). The Prophet told her: "I see you have become unlawful to him." She pleaded repeatedly with Allah: "O Allah, to You alone I complain of my destitution and separation from my children!" Allah immediately revealed: "Allah has indeed heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband..." abolishing zihar and instituting expiation.

58:8.occasion: The Jews, who had a treaty with the Prophet (peace be upon him), would hold secret counsels when a Muslim passed by their gathering, making him fear they were plotting to harm him. Though warned to stop, they persisted, and this verse was revealed about them. They would also greet the Prophet by twisting the greeting into 'As-Sam alayka' (death be upon you), saying within themselves that Allah would have punished them if he were truly a Prophet.
58:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

58:22.occasion: This verse is reported to have been revealed concerning Abu 'Ubaydah 'Amir bin Al-Jarrah, who killed his disbelieving father at the battle of Badr, showing that true believers do not befriend those who oppose Allah and His Messenger even if they are close kin.
58:22.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that this surah was revealed concerning the Jewish tribe of Bani An-Nadir. After they betrayed their treaty with the Prophet and plotted to kill him by dropping a stone on him while he sat by a wall of their houses, he laid siege to their forts and they were exiled from Al-Madinah, leaving their homes and wealth behind.
59:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:9.occasion: A poor man came to the Prophet complaining of hunger, and an Ansari (named in another narration as Abu Talhah) took him home; finding only food for the children, he and his wife put the children to sleep hungry and turned off the lamp so the guest could eat. The next morning the Prophet said Allah was pleased with their action, and this verse praising those who give others preference over themselves was revealed.
59:9.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

59:11.occasion: Ibn Kathir states that this passage was revealed about the hypocrites, such as Abdullah bin Ubayy and those like him, who sent word to Bani An-Nadir falsely promising that they would go out with them if they were expelled and help them if they were attacked, a promise they never intended to keep.
59:11.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir states the opening of the surah was revealed concerning Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) prepared to march on Makkah, Hatib secretly sent a letter with a woman warning the Quraysh of the planned attack, hoping they would protect his family there. The Prophet was informed, the letter was intercepted, and Hatib's excuse was accepted, after which these verses came down.
60:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:8.occasion: Asma' bint Abi Bakr's mother Qutaylah, who was still an idolatress, came to her with gifts during the period of the treaty with Quraysh. Asma' refused to receive her or accept the gifts and asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) through 'A'ishah, whereupon this verse was revealed permitting kind and just treatment of disbelievers who do not fight the believers over religion, and the Prophet ordered her to receive her mother.
60:8.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

60:10.occasion: After the treaty of Al-Hudaybiyyah, which stipulated that anyone coming over to the Muslims be returned, believing women began emigrating to Madinah. When Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah emigrated and her brothers came demanding her return, Allah revealed this verse exempting the women from the treaty, commanding that their faith be tested and that they not be sent back to the disbelievers.
60:10.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

61:2.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Muqatil bin Hayyan that the believers had said that if they only knew the dearest deeds to Allah they would perform them; they were then tested on the day of Uhud, where they retreated and fled, leaving the Prophet (peace be upon him) behind, and it was concerning their case that this verse was revealed. He also cites Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak that it was sent down to rebuke people who falsely claimed they had fought, killed, and stabbed in battle when they had done none of it.
61:2.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

63:5.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that several of the Salaf held this passage was revealed concerning Abdullah bin Ubay bin Salul. According to Qatadah and As-Suddi, after a young relative conveyed an awful statement of his to the Prophet (peace be upon him), Abdullah swore he had not said it; when invited to come so the Messenger might seek forgiveness for him, he turned his head away and refused.
63:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

72:16.occasion: Muqatil reported that this verse was revealed concerning the disbelievers of the Quraysh at the time when they had been deprived of rain for seven years.
72:16.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

72:18.occasion: Ibn Jarir reported from Sa'id bin Jubayr that the Jinn asked the Prophet how they could come to the Masjid and be present for the prayer when they were so far away from him, whereupon Allah revealed this verse declaring that the Masjids belong to Allah, so none should be invoked along with Him.
72:18.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

74:24.occasion: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah entered the house of Abu Bakr and asked about the Qur'an, then told the Quraysh that it was not poetry, magic, or madness but the Word of Allah. The Quraysh feared his conversion would lead all of them to convert, so Abu Jahl went to him and provoked him by claiming his people said he only visited Abu Bakr to get his food. Al-Walid then declared the Qur'an to be merely 'inherited magic of old,' and Allah revealed the passage beginning 'Leave Me alone with whom I created lonely' through 'It spares not, nor does it leave.'
74:24.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

75:34.occasion: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took hold of Abu Jahl and said to him, "Woe to you, and then woe to you! Again woe to you, and then woe to you!" Allah then revealed this verse.
75:34.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

80:1.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that while the Messenger of Allah was earnestly speaking with one of the great leaders of the Quraysh, hoping he would accept Islam, the blind man Ibn Umm Maktum, an early Muslim, came urgently asking to be taught. The Prophet frowned and turned away from him to continue with the noble man, and these verses were revealed reproving that and commanding that warning be given equally to noble and weak alike. Ibn Kathir also cites 'A'ishah that the passage was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man, who came saying 'Guide me' while a great idolater leader was present.
80:1.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

81:29.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports that when the verse "To whomsoever among you who wills to walk straight" (81:28) was revealed, Abu Jahl said that the matter was up to them, that they would stand straight if they wished and would not if they did not wish. Allah then revealed, "And you cannot will unless that Allah wills, the Lord of all that exists" (81:29).
81:29.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

82:6.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Al-Baghawi that Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said this verse, 'What has made you careless about your Lord, the Most Generous?', was revealed concerning Al-Aswad bin Shariq, who struck the Prophet and was not punished in retaliation, whereupon Allah revealed it.
82:6.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

85:4.occasion: Ibn Kathir relates from Ibn Ishaq's Sirah that these verses were revealed concerning the People of the Ditch, identified as Dhu Nuwas (Yusuf, son of Tuban As'ad Abi Karib) and his army, who called the believing Christians of Najran to abandon their faith for Judaism. When they refused, he had ditches dug and burned and killed about twenty thousand of them, and it was about this that Allah revealed verses 85:4-9.
85:4.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

89:27.occasion: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Abbas that this verse about the tranquil soul was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him). Abu Bakr said, 'O Messenger of Allah, there is nothing better than this,' and the Prophet replied that this would indeed be said to him.
89:27.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

92:5.occasion: Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Amir bin 'Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr that Abu Bakr used to free weak servants, the elderly, and women in Makkah when they accepted Islam. When his father urged him instead to free strong men who could defend him, Abu Bakr replied that he sought only what is with Allah. Some of his family said this Ayah was revealed concerning him.
92:5.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

92:17.occasion: Many of the scholars of Tafsir mentioned that these Ayat were revealed about Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, and some even reported a consensus on this. He was foremost in giving his wealth in obedience to Allah and in aiding the Messenger of Allah, seeking only the Face of his Lord and expecting no favor in return.
92:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

93:1.occasion: Revelation ceased for a period of several days or weeks, causing the Prophet ﷺ deep anxiety. A pagan woman (Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab) taunted him saying: "O Muhammad! I see that your devil has forsaken you and despises you!" In response to this cruelty and to comfort His beloved Messenger, Allah revealed Surah ad-Duha: "By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers with darkness, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor does He hate you."

96:9.occasion: This was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened the Prophet (peace be upon him) and tried to prevent him from praying at the Ka'bah.
96:9.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

96:17.occasion: Abu Jahl threatened the Prophet (peace be upon him) while he prayed near the Station of Ibrahim, boasting that he had the most supporters of anyone in the valley. In response Allah revealed the command for him to call upon his council, while Allah would call the guards of Hell.
96:17.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

108:1.occasion: When the infant son of the Prophet ﷺ, al-Qasim (and later Abdullah), passed away in Makkah, al-As ibn Wa'il and other Quraysh leaders gloated and mocked him, saying: "Muhammad is 'abtar' (cut off from lineage, without male heir to carry his name; he will be forgotten when he dies)." Allah revealed Surah al-Kawthar to comfort the Prophet: "Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar (abundant good and a river in Paradise)... Indeed, your enemy is the one who is cut off."

108:3.occasion: According to 'Ata', the Surah was revealed about Abu Lahab. When a son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died, Abu Lahab went to the idolators and said that Muhammad had been cut off (from progeny) that night.
108:3.source: As cited by Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Adhim

111:1.occasion: When the command came to warn his closest kinsmen (26:214), the Prophet ﷺ climbed Mount Safa and called out the clans of Quraysh by name until they gathered. He asked: "If I told you that horsemen were emerging from the foot of this mountain to attack you, would you believe me?" They answered: "Yes, we have known you only as truthful." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." His uncle Abu Lahab shouted: "Tabban lak! (May you perish!) Is it for this that you gathered us?" Allah immediately revealed Surah al-Masad: "May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and ruined is he!"
